title: Nvidia Restricts Capacity for Chinese Clients in New Cloud GPU Deals
summary:
The chipmaker has mandated that cloud providers reserve a majority of their hardware for customers outside of China to hinder the evasion of trade bans on advanced semiconductors. New contracts must designate at least 51% of GPU services to non-Chinese clients, a measure intended to curb the use of overseas data centers as a workaround for U.S. export controls. Washington is considering further legislation to close the current regulatory gap that allows Chinese firms to rent remote access to chips held abroad.

The restrictions follow reports that the developer of the Kimi AI model, Moonshot AI, sought to lease clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs from cloud providers in Europe. To mitigate the risk of future sanctions, the lab reportedly offered to pay 30% to 50% more in upfront costs than customers based outside China. In July, the White House alleged that Moonshot had already used a similar loop hole to access Blackwell hardware through a facility in Thailand.

MOONSHOT SEEKS $NVDA BLACKWELL ACCESS IN EUROPE

Chinese AI lab Moonshot, the developer of Kimi, has held talks to rent clusters of 8,000+ Nvidia Blackwell GPUs from European 🇪🇺 neoclouds, primarily for inference and potentially training, CNBC reports.

The White House previously accused Moonshot of accessing Blackwell chips remotely through a data center in Thailand.

U.S. export controls restrict shipments of these chips to China, but don't broadly prohibit Chinese companies from renting the same computing power through overseas cloud providers.

One proposed arrangement reportedly involved Moonshot paying 30%-50% more upfront than non-Chinese customers, reflecting the risk of future restrictions.

No completed deal has been confirmed.

selectedTweets.text:
CNBC: Moonshot AI, the Chinese lab behind Kimi, has sought to rent Nvidia Blackwell chips in European data centers.

It discussed deals with neoclouds, non-Chinese GPU rental firms that can buy the hardware.

U.S. export controls bar shipping those chips to China but don’t broadly cover renting them from servers abroad.

The White House accused Moonshot in July of using the same route in Thailand, and a source said the European talks came afterward.

One person described clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs, sought mainly for serving Kimi to users.

Under one proposed lease, Moonshot would pay 30% to 50% more upfront than a non-Chinese renter, cushioning neoclouds if Washington bans remote access.

Nvidia reportedly told cloud providers that on new contracts, at least 51% of services must go to non-Chinese customers.

That cap still leaves 49% for Chinese buyers, letting a large European neocloud rent Moonshot 8,000 GPUs.
